clause.quote: If the second character is not a letter but is a numeral `0` - `9` or `-` or `_`, then it MUST be either a selector for a different Count Code table or an error.

inferred_from.inference: A parser should reject a count code whose second character is a numeral selecting no table the genus defines; the clause calls such a code an error but does not say what a parser does with it.

description: After a KERI 2.0 inception, the attachment position holds the count code -0AB, whose second character is the numeral 0. The specification reserves numerals for other count code tables and genus 2.00 defines none, so the code is an error. (keripy 1.x used -0 as its big-count selector; genus 2.00 uses --.) The clause calls the code an error but does not say what a parser does with it, so the assertion that a parser rejects the stream is graded SHOULD on the inference recorded in inferred_from.
title: Reject an attachment count code whose second character selects no defined table
